newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnlines CEO sees good outlook for BTL.
newsitem.headline: Finnlines CEO sees good outlook for BTL.

text.p: Finnish cargo shipping group Finnlines Oy chief executive Antti Lagerroos said on Tuesday the outlook for Swedish transport and logistics group BTL was very good.

"The outlook for the future of BTL is very good," Lagerroos, a member of the BTL board, told Reuters by telephone. He did not elaborate, but said BTL was market leader in Sweden and Finland, and strong also in other countries around the Baltic Sea.
Lagerroos declined to comment on Finnlines' strategic aims in acquiring options to increase its ownership in Bilspedition Transport & Logistics AB to 45 percent of votes from 25 percent.
He confirmed media reports that Finnlines had taken the initiative to acquire the options, which are in force until March 1997. "It was our initiative, that is all I have to say."

In response to a question, he said it was "an interesting idea" that Finnlines might be aiming to become the leading sea and land cargo transporting group in the Baltic Sea region, but he underlined that "shipping is our core business".
Lagerroos said it was positive that trade in Finnlines shares on the Helsinki bourse had been active in recent days. He said he knew who had been buying and selling.
Asked whether he was pleased with that knowledge, he said: "Yes", but declined to elaborate.
At 1620/1320 GMT, Finnlines traded 3.90 markka or four percent higher at 101.00 markka after touching a 22-month high 103.00 markka. Volume was very active at more than 111,000 shares.
